summary: First and third-person player camera with collision, smoothing and FOV boost. No rig hierarchy to build.
overview: Drop it on a Camera, assign the player, pick a mode. There is no pivot hierarchy to construct because position is computed from the target plus yaw, pitch and distance rather than from parented objects — which is also why switching between first and third person is just a mode change.
useCases: A third-person character camera that pulls in when a wall would block it.
First-person with the target turning to face the camera's yaw.
Switching between the two at runtime without rebuilding anything.

params.tuning: Leave foliage, props and small clutter OUT, or the camera lurches forward every time a blade of grass crosses the line.
It spherecasts rather than raycasts so thin geometry and corners cannot slip through. Roughly the camera's near-plane size is a sensible starting point.
The floor the collision pull-in respects. Too small and the camera ends up inside the character.
Frame-rate independent, like the follow camera. Higher is snappier.
Standard for first person, usually wrong for third — it stops the character being able to face away from the camera.
A small amount reads as speed. More than a few degrees reads as a fisheye.
Head bob. Worth exposing as an accessibility option — it makes some players motion sick.

gotchas.title: Pitch clamps, yaw does not
gotchas.body: minPitch and maxPitch stop the camera flipping over. Yaw wraps freely, which is what you want, but means a raw yaw value grows without bound.

gotchas.title: lockCursor makes the Editor awkward
gotchas.body: It hides and locks the cursor to the window, which is right in a build and irritating while testing. Escape releases it in the Editor.
